svg.title: A 30-year-old woman is brought in by police after threatening neighbors with a knife. She refuses evaluation and tries to walk out. She is shouting, pacing, and has thrown a chair. Verbal de-escalation and an offer of oral medication have both failed. The provider writes an order for physical restraint for violent behavior.
svg.desc: Emergency psychiatric holds are created by state statute, and states differ on the permitted length, the criteria, and who is allowed to initiate one, so her state's law and the facility policy give the specific answer. The Medicare conditions of participation cap renewal of a violent-behavior restraint order at 4 hours for adults 18 and older, 2 hours for ages 9 through 17, and 1 hour under age 9, for up to 24 hours total, with a face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour of initiation. A relative cannot consent to detain another adult, and waiting for a court order would leave an actively dangerous situation unmanaged.
